summary: Ichiro Hori was a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. Educated at the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo, he also studied under Kunio Yanagita. He taught at Tohoku University and the University of Tokyo.

Ichiro Katayama is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa and Otani universities under Kogen Mizuno. He was an associate professor (1975) and professor (1985–2013) at Komazawa University, and headed the Society for the Study of Pali and Buddhist Culture.

Ichiro Numata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. By 2026, he held posts as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Ignazio Guidi worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the Sapienza University of Rome, where he subsequently served as a professor from 1876 to 1919.

Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov was an Indologist who studied philology at Saint Petersburg State University from 1936 to 1941. He worked for Pravda (~1952–1956) and was later affiliated with the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1960–1998).

Ihsan Ali is an archaeologist who studied at the University of Peshawar and under Frank Raymond Allchin. He held posts as professor at the University of Peshawar (~1998), director of KP Archaeology and Museums (~2002–2006), and vice chancellor of Hazara University (~2006–2009).

Ikko Arai is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Komazawa University. He studied under Shiro Matsumoto, Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen, Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.
Ikuhisa Takigawa is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. In 2002, he held posts as a part-time lecturer at both Waseda University and Tokai University.
Ikuko Tazaki works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2017, she held research posts at both Otani University and Kyoto University.

Ikuro Hattori works in Indology and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the University of Pune and held posts at Toho Kenkyukai (attested 2003), the Eastern Institute (attested 2026), and Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2026).

Ilkka Pyysiäinen is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who studied under Juha Pentikäinen, René Gothóni, and Simo Knuuttila. He served as an Academy Research Fellow at the University of Helsinki (1984) and visited Oxford (~2007–2008).

Immanuel Kant was a philosopher who was educated at Collegium Fridericianum and the University of Königsberg (1740–1746). He was appointed to the chair of logic and metaphysics at the University of Königsberg in 1770.

Imran Philip is a researcher in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under doctoral supervisor Kaustubh Mani Sengupta. He was awarded a Dr. Zakir Hussain Fellowship at the Asiatic Society, attested in 2026.

Imre Bangha is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Visva-Bharati University. He has served as Associate Professor of Hindi at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College since circa 2003, and honorary professor at ELTE (~2017).

Imre Galambos is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. Educated at ELTE, Nankai University, and UC Berkeley (PhD), he held posts at the British Library, the University of Cambridge (2012–2023), and Zhejiang University (~2023).

Imre Hamar is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Eötvös Loránd University, National Taiwan Normal University, and under Noritoshi Aramaki. He became a professor at Eötvös Loránd University (~2006) and director of its Confucius Institute (2006).

In-gun Kang is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, Jesuit School of Theology of Santa Clara University, and under Michael Barnes at Heythrop College, University of London.

Ines Konczak specializes in history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She has held posts as a postdoctoral research fellow at the Berlin State Museums and as a visiting research fellow at Ryukoku University (2012).

Ingmar Heise is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA in Chinese Studies at Leiden University in 2005 and later pursued doctoral studies at the University of Bristol (attested 2012).

Ingo Strauch is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the Free University of Berlin in 2000 and served as a professor at the University of Lausanne (attested 2018).
